title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: these are notes continuing 'La Longue Marche'. The previous page asked when a homomorphism G_a -> GL_n of the form λ ↦ exp(λX), with X nilpotent, defined only where certain integers are invertible, extends over the whole base, possibly after rescaling. It already stated a corollary for p-power rescaling when S is local of residue characteristic p. This page states the general version.

PROPOSITION (stated as a proposition, though the words read as 'on va conjecturer[?]').
- S is a noetherian (quasi-compact) prescheme and n ≥ 1 an integer.
- S_0 = V(n·1_S) is the closed subscheme where n = 0. Pointwise, x ∈ S_0 iff char k(x) divides n.
- U = S \ S_0 is assumed schematically dense in S. Equivalently, n is locally a non-zero-divisor on O_S.
- G is an affine S-group scheme and φ_U : G_{a,U} -> G_U is a homomorphism of U-group schemes.
- Claim: there is a power m = n^r and a homomorphism of S-group schemes ψ_m : G_a -> G with ψ_m|U = φ_U ∘ u_m. Here u_m : λ ↦ mλ, so ψ_m(λ) = φ_U(mλ) = φ_U(λ)^m.

Reformulation: the claim says the composite φ_U ∘ u_m : G_{a,U} -> G_U extends to a homomorphism G_a -> G for m a large power of n. Grothendieck draws a commutative triangle to express this.

PROOF (begun on the next page, p.655).
- By schematic density and uniqueness, it suffices to extend φ_U ∘ u_m as a morphism of schemes. The group-homomorphism property then follows automatically, since G_a ×_S G_a restricted to U is schematically dense.
- Locally S = Spec A and G = Spec B. Then U = Spec A_n with A_n = A[1/n], and φ_U corresponds to ψ : B ⊗_A A_n -> A_n[T].
- Composing with u_m^* : T ↦ mT sends x = Σ a_i T^i (a_i ∈ A_n) to Σ m^i a_i T^i.
- Denominators are powers of n, so for m = n^ν large every m^i a_i with i ≥ 1 lies in A. Hence u_m^*ψ(x) ∈ A[T] iff a_0 ∈ A.
- a_0 is ψ(x) evaluated at T = 0, i.e. the counit ε_G(x). This lies in A because the unit section of G is defined over S.
- Apply this to finitely many A-algebra generators of B to get one m. Quasi-compactness of S gives a uniform m, and density gives gluing.

Purpose: this is the denominator-clearing step for extending exponential-type homomorphisms G_a -> G across bad characteristics after rescaling. The isolated hard case left on the previous page is the n = 5 nilpotent-matrix question (20).
errors: The argument needs G of finite type (finitely presented) over S, so that finitely many generators of B require a common m. For a general affine G (B not finitely generated) the required power of n could be unbounded. 'Affine' alone, as written, is not enough.
Schematic density of U is necessary: A -> A[1/n] must be injective for uniqueness and for the 'automatically a homomorphism' step. It was correctly added as an afterthought.

Notational: the diagonal arrow in the triangle is labelled ψ_U, while in the statement the map is ψ_m (restricted to U). Writing φ_U(λ)^m uses multiplicative notation in G; this is fine but G need not be commutative. It is harmless since only powers of a single element occur.

The remark 'Quand G est affine, ceci devrait être trivial' is right only modulo the finite-type hypothesis. Non-affine G (e.g. non-separated or with non-affine fibres) is where real difficulty would lie, and this is not addressed on this page.

ideas.what: Extension of a homomorphism G_a -> G defined over S[1/n] to all of S after precomposing with multiplication by a large power of n (clearing denominators via the grading of A[T]).
ideas.modern_name: Integral models of homomorphisms / denominator clearing for G_a-actions (rescaling a G_a-action); cf. extension of morphisms over schematically dense opens
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; standard in SGA3-style arguments and in literature on integral exponentials and unipotent elements in bad characteristic
ideas.where_published: Similar density/extension arguments appear in SGA3 (Exp. on G_a-actions, schematic density) and EGA IV §11 / §20, but this exact statement is not known to me.

ideas.what: Stratifying the base by V(n) (points of residue characteristic dividing n) and treating φ on the complement as a homomorphism to be extended after twisting by u_m.
ideas.modern_name: Spreading out over Z[1/n] and extending over bad primes

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, essentially routine lemma (rescaled extension of G_a-homomorphisms across V(n)), with a correct proof modulo the finite-type hypothesis. It is a technical step toward the exponential/nilpotent question of the previous page and contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'On va conjecturer[?]' is uncertain; the scrawl may rather read 'On va voir que' or similar, and what follows is labelled 'Proposition' and is proved on the next page.
The bracketed 'car x | n' insertion means: x ∈ S_0 iff char k(x) divides n. The 'de f.f.[?]' fragment is illegible and probably part of a struck phrase.
In (22) the right-hand side reads 'φ_U^m : λ ↦ φ_U(mλ) = φ_U(λ)^m'.
The diagonal arrow label in the diagram is 'ψ_U' (as in the image).
